# @metator/plugin-codehost-mcp

## Responsibility

The `CodeHost` and `ReviewHost` ports over MCP (T2, T3, design/14 §3–4, ADR-0083): lists the items of an intake source (GitHub or GitLab issues, Jira) and the review threads of pull (merge) requests through the MCP server configured under `mcp:`; replies to a thread and resolves it when core says so (`McpReviewHost`). It maps a source to one tool call (`listCall`) and the server's JSON to `IntakeItem`s (`itemsFromResult`); `SdkToolCaller` is the only part that talks to a server. It decides nothing about issues, runs or limits (that is core's `ScanIntake` and `MyReviews`); it writes to a host only through `reply` and `resolve`, which core calls after a person's decision.

## Invariants

- A pull request listed among issues is not a task [[cite: packages/plugin-codehost-mcp/src/mcp-code-host.ts:78 | "if (entry.pull_request !== undefined) continue;"]].
- The server is the one the rule names, or the one named like the source's kind [[cite: packages/plugin-codehost-mcp/src/mcp-code-host.ts:113 | "const name = source.mcp ?? source.kind;"]].
- A connection lives for one call and is closed after it, also on failure [[cite: packages/plugin-codehost-mcp/src/sdk-tool-caller.ts:60 | "await client.close().catch(() => undefined);"]].

## Allowed dependencies

`@metator/core` and the MCP SDK client (`@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`, ADR-0081); `@metator/testing` in tests. Nothing else: no other plugin, not the runtime.

## Pitfalls

- Servers name their tools differently (`list_issues`, `jira_search`, …): the usual one per kind is a default, a rule's `source.tool` overrides it.
- A tool's result is text that holds JSON; anything else is `PARSE_FAILED`, never a throw.
- The text of an item is the reporter's: it is data for a task, never instructions.
